cands.name: DeAndrea Salvador
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina Senate for District 39 (Mecklenburg County) since January 2021. Founder and CEO of the nonprofit Renewable Energy Transition Initiative (RETI), 2018 TED Fellow, and a data-privacy professional. Helped negotiate the energy law HB 951.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among her 2026 endorsements.

cands.gaps: The pages we had did not give her birthplace or the year she came to North Carolina; the "lifelong resident" claim comes from her own campaign site. We found no stated positions or documented actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented stance on data centers or development, and no controversies or foreign ties. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year, and her campaign site lists priorities (affordable healthcare, educational opportunity, infrastructure, energy and environment) without specific policy commitments.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site calls her a fifth-generation Charlottean and a lifelong District 39 resident, and Ballotpedia lists a Charlotte high school and UNC Charlotte degree, but no page gives her birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2021 (re-elected 2022, 2024 and 2026). Founded and led the RETI nonprofit from 2014. Works in data privacy and is a Certified Information Privacy Professional. Served on the Mecklenburg County Air Quality Commission. Took part in negotiating HB 951.
qual.why: Five-plus years of prior legislative service plus policy work on energy legislation put her in the high band. Board, commission and committee seats were not counted.
